title: Films true to the text
statement: A film about a text says only what the text supports, with no labels for its characters that the text doesn't bear out.
detail: A content review of a reference lesson found its introductory films calling three characters heroes when none of them is, and the course made factual accuracy about the text a criterion; one lesson's film transcript was then audited for such labels and matched the passage (`grade3-reading/artifacts/criteria-register.csv`, line 109). A draft plan for another opening film carries the same boundary (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/video-2026-09-16/PETER-PAN-PART-1-FILM.md`, line 79).

evidence.quote: Videos must be factually accurate about the text; Aladdin, Peter Pan and Toad are NOT heroes and must not be called that
Character identity and setting must be checked during academic and visual review; the final cuts should be revised if they imply a character is present in a scene where the play does not place them.
Faces and surroundings carry meaning; captions identify only people, place, or established facts.
